newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan waives 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Jordan waives 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling.

text.p: Jordan's top investment body approved late on Monday a decision to scrap a 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling on most publicly listed stocks, officials said on Tuesday.
Banks, telecommunications, transport, and insurance will all now be allowed 100 percent foreign ownership, they said.

Deputy Prime Minister Jawad Anani, who heads the higher investment council which approved scrapping the ceiling, told Reuters the move was designed to attract foreign investment. The decision must be approved by the Jordanian cabinet, officials said.
Three sectors - construction, general retail trade and mining - were excluded from the new ruling and will be reviewed at a later date.
The mining sector includes the strategic potash and phophates industries which already have substantial Arab governmental holdings.
The removal of foreign ownership limits went far beyond investor expectations of a slight lifting to around 70 percent.
Jordan has been mulling the changes as part of efforts to attract investment enabling the state to go ahead in wider state sell-off of its majority stakes in leading firms.
Analysts said the ruling should attract more global fund buying in Amman's financial markets.

The changes also include a minimum 50,000 dinars ($70,000) level of foreign investment in small service oriented ventures until now restricted to Jordanians. -- Amman newsroom +9626 623 776 ($ = 0.708 Jordanian Dinars)
